events.title: Audit Finding
events.text: Internal audit has flagged an unmanaged exception on a critical system: a legacy service that bypasses your MFA policy.

choices.result: You pay for the fix and tighten a control while you are at it.
choices.lesson: Closing the finding removes a real path; budget it as risk reduction, not overhead.

choices.result: You bank the saving and sign the exception. The risk is now yours.
choices.lesson: Risk acceptance is legitimate when explicit, time-boxed and owned by someone with authority.

events.lesson: Exceptions that nobody reviews become the attack path.

events.title: Zero-Day in the VPN Appliance
events.text: A vendor advisory lands at 02:10: an edge appliance you run is being exploited in the wild. No patch yet.

choices.text: Take it offline until a patch ships
choices.result: Staff lose remote access for two days — painful, but nobody is in your network.
choices.lesson: When exploitation is active and no patch exists, removing exposure is the control.

choices.text: Apply the vendor’s mitigation and watch closely
choices.result: You deploy virtual patching and add monitoring.
choices.lesson: Mitigations buy time; verify them and hunt for prior compromise.

choices.result: Nothing happens… that you can see. Your next fight starts with an intruder already inside.
choices.lesson: Known-exploited edge devices are a favourite of state actors: assume compromise if you could not patch.

events.lesson: Edge devices are repeatedly exploited as initial access; ASD/CISA advisories are the early warning.

events.title: Staff Report a Phish
events.text: A finance officer reported a convincing invoice email in minutes — the SOC has triaged and blocked it.

choices.result: Reporting culture strengthens. Next battle you start with extra intelligence.
choices.lesson: People who report quickly are a sensor network; punishing clicks silences it.

choices.result: Efficient. Also forgettable.

events.lesson: Make reporting easy, rewarded and blame-free.

events.title: The Silver-Bullet Pitch
events.text: A vendor promises an “AI-native autonomous SOC” that makes detection engineering unnecessary.

choices.result: You get a powerful tool and an integration headache.
choices.lesson: Tools do not remove the need to engineer detections and own the outcomes.

choices.result: The pilot sharpens an existing control and teaches your team where the gaps are.
choices.lesson: Proofs of value with success criteria beat roadmap promises.

choices.result: You keep the budget for people and process.

events.lesson: Evaluate tools against the techniques you actually face.

events.title: Regulator Information Request
events.text: A regulator asks for evidence of your incident notification procedure and last test.

choices.text: Respond fully and share your last exercise report
choices.result: It takes your team away from the console, but the exercise findings drive real changes.
choices.lesson: Evidence of exercising is evidence of capability. In Australia obligations differ by sector — e.g. SOCI critical-infrastructure reporting and APRA CPS 234 notification.

choices.result: You save effort now and create a follow-up later.

events.lesson: Know your notification clocks before the incident.

events.title: MSP Offers “Free” Remote Access
events.text: Your managed service provider wants always-on, privileged remote access “to speed up tickets”, at a discount.

choices.result: Costs fall. A third party now holds standing admin into your estate.
choices.lesson: Trusted relationships are a documented initial access path.

choices.result: The MSP grumbles but complies.
choices.lesson: Vendor access should be time-boxed, MFA-gated and logged.

events.lesson: Third-party access is your attack surface.

events.title: Security Awareness Week
events.text: You can run a company-wide awareness and phishing-simulation week.

choices.result: Productivity dips slightly; click rates drop.
choices.lesson: Training is a layer, not a wall.

choices.result: You save the time.

events.title: Backup Restore Test
events.text: It is time for the quarterly restore test of your critical systems.

choices.text: Run a full restore in a sandbox
choices.result: You find out what really works.
choices.lesson: A backup you have not restored is a hope. The test either upgrades your confidence or exposes the gap.

choices.result: The dashboard is green. Is the data?

events.lesson: Test restoration, not just backup jobs.

events.title: Bug Bounty Submission
events.text: A researcher has reported a serious flaw in your customer portal and asks for a bounty and a public thank-you.

choices.text: Pay and fix within a week
choices.result: You close the hole and build goodwill.
choices.lesson: Coordinated disclosure only works if researchers are treated well.

choices.result: The researcher goes public. So does everyone else.
choices.lesson: Hostile responses push findings to the open market.

events.lesson: Make it safe to tell you about your bugs.

events.title: Merger: Integrate the Acquisition
events.text: You have acquired a smaller firm. Leadership wants the networks joined by Friday.

choices.result: A flat, unmapped network and two new problems.
choices.lesson: M&A inherits risk; integrate through a segmented, monitored interconnect.

choices.text: Phase it: segment, assess, then connect
choices.result: Slower and safer.

events.title: Executive Tabletop
events.text: The executive team agrees to a half-day tabletop on a ransomware scenario.

choices.result: Decision rights, comms and legal triggers all get tested.
choices.lesson: Executives who have rehearsed the decisions make them faster under pressure.

choices.result: Everyone is relieved.

events.lesson: Exercise the decisions, not just the tooling.

events.title: Insider Tip-off
events.text: An anonymous message warns that a contractor has been selling access to your VPN.

choices.text: Reset all contractor credentials and review access
choices.result: Disruptive, but you find two dormant accounts.
choices.lesson: Dormant and shared accounts are routinely sold: valid accounts is the most reused technique.

choices.result: Quiet… for now.

events.lesson: Valid accounts are the quiet way in.
